subject.title: [Feature]: Memory indexing lacks checkpoint/resume capability for long-running operations

question: Should memory-core implement resumable full reindexing as a validated resumable shadow generation, direct incremental live-DB writes, or defer checkpoint/resume support for now?
rationale: Source inspection proves the reliability gap, but durable generation identity, incomplete-index search/status behavior, orphan cleanup policy, and any public `memorySearch` configuration are product/API decisions rather than a strict mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Approve resumable shadow generation
options.body: Persist generation/checkpoint state for the shadow DB and publish only after validation, preserving the current known-good-index invariant while allowing restart resume.

options.title: Use direct incremental live writes
options.body: Write checkpointed progress into the live DB with explicit incomplete-generation filtering and status semantics, accepting a larger migration and compatibility surface.

options.title: Defer resume support
options.body: Keep atomic full rebuild behavior and rely on cache reuse, retry, and orphan cleanup until maintainers prioritize a broader memory indexing redesign.

recommendation.title: Approve resumable shadow generation
recommendation.body: Persist generation/checkpoint state for the shadow DB and publish only after validation, preserving the current known-good-index invariant while allowing restart resume.

likelyOwner.reason: The earlier reindex lineage and prior keep-open review route the product-shape decision most directly to steipete, with vincentkoc as a likely implementation owner for the current SQLite/reindex path.
